info.bio:
Oasis fue una banda británica de rock formada en Mánchester en 1991. Inicialmente conocida como The Rain, la banda estaba formada por el cantante Liam Gallagher, el guitarrista Paul Arthurs, el bajista Paul McGuigan y el baterista Tony McCarroll, a los que más tarde se uniría como compositor y guitarrista principal el hermano mayor de Liam, Noel Gallagher.

Musicalmente sus principales influencias fueron, según ellos mismos, The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, The Stone Roses y The Who.

scenes.name: Brit-pop y post-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como tantas veces, el fenómeno más publicitado es el menos interesante: un «brit-pop» de grupos terriblemente parecidos y tediosos, sin apenas imaginación. Lo anticipan Lightning Seeds, La's, Teenage Fanclub y Heavenly; estalla con Boo Radleys, Blur (Parklife) y Oasis (el «farol» que mejor personifica la moda). Suede y el glam-pop (Super Furry Animals, Placebo), las excepciones de High Llamas (Hawaii) y Supergrass, el revival mod (Ocean Colour Scene, Wildhearts), Elastica, Sleeper, las Spice Girls; Trembling Blue Stars, Tindersticks, Delgados. El post-pop de Radiohead, «la banda más publicitada y sobrevalorada de la década», cuyo OK Computer es una obra maestra del falso vanguardismo; Coldplay, Travis.

podcast.title: Noel Gallagher Joins Rain, Band Becomes Oasis (1991)
podcast.body: After a gig by Liam's band Rain in 1991, Liam and his bandmates asked Noel to manage them. Noel declined the management offer but instead proposed joining as their lead guitarist, citing his years of songwriting and the superior quality of his material compared to Rain's songs. The band accepted, initiating the transformation of Rain into Oasis. "The van accepted, and that's when Rain started the Metamorphosis into Oasis."

podcast.title: Discovery at King Tut's Wah Wah Hut (1993)
podcast.body: On May 31, 1993, Oasis, referred to as "a bunch of Yabo's from Manchester," performed an unscheduled four-song set at King Tut's Wah Wah Hut in Glasgow. Alan McGee, head of Creation Records, was in the audience due to a mix-up in set times and, after hearing only those four songs, immediately offered them a deal with his indie label. "a bunch of Yabo's from Manchester who bullied their way on stage at a venue called King Tuts Wawa Hut in Glasgow. That was May 31, 1993. They played four songs, and in the audience that night was Alan McGee, the head of creation records. All it took though was those four songs. He offered them a deal with creation, an indie label."

"Oasis was discovered by Alan McGee of creation records after they allegedly threatened the owner with arson if he didn't let them play that night."

podcast.title: Discovery by Creation Records and Sony Acquisition (1993)
podcast.body: Oasis was initially discovered and championed in 1993 by Creation Records, an independent label known for breaking acts like My Bloody Valentine. Crucially, Sony acquired Creation Records precisely as Oasis's recording contract was being finalized, granting the band immediate access to the significant promotional and financial resources of Sony Music for their launch. "Sony compro clientes son recursos justo al tiempo en el que estaban firmando el contrato escoráfico de oasis."

podcast.body: In early 1993, Oasis had played only 10 gigs and were attempting to assemble enough material for a show in Liverpool scheduled four weeks later. "A new group called Oasis had played all of 10 gigs and were trying to pull together enough material for a show in 4 weeks in Liverpool."

podcast.title: Forced Performance and Record Deal at King Tuts Wawa Hut (May 31, 1993)
podcast.body: On Sunday, May 31, 1993, Oasis, who were not scheduled to play, physically "bullied their way on stage" for a set at King Tuts Wawa Hut in Glasgow, Scotland. Having hitched a ride with another Manchester group, 18 Wheeler, they threatened the venue's owner and bouncers with burning down the club if they weren't allowed to perform. Coincidentally, Alan McGee of Creation Records was present, initially to see other bands on the bill, but was so impressed by Oasis that he signed them "more or less on the spot," later lending them £1,000 for equipment. "Oasis literally bullied their way on stage for a set at King Tuts Wawa Hut in Glasgow, Scotland."

podcast.title: Noel Gallagher's "Coup d'Etat" (Spring 1993)
podcast.body: In the spring of 1993, after being fired from his job as a guitar roadie with the Inspiral Carpets and left with only £2,000 in severance pay, Noel Gallagher was determined to forge a proper music career. While impressed by his younger brother Liam's band, he offered to join on the strict condition, effectively a "coup d'etat," that he be "in charge of everything" within the group. "I will join your group, he said, but you have to let me be in charge of everything."

podcast.title: Rapid Ascent to Stardom (1993-1994)
podcast.body: Oasis experienced an exceptionally rapid rise to fame, transitioning from unknown to superstars within months of their discovery in 1993. This swift progression contrasted sharply with bands like Pulp, Suede, and Blur, who endured years, or even a decade, of development before achieving widespread recognition. "oasis en casi unos meses de ser descubiertos a ser super estrellas no pasan casi unos meses."

podcast.title: Crystal Meth Use on First North American Tour (1994)
podcast.body: During their first North American tour, the entire band, including Noel and Liam Gallagher, was heavily using crystal meth. This drug use contributed to the intense conflicts and instability that led to Noel temporarily leaving the tour after the Whisky a Go-Go incident. "What wasn't mentioned at the time was how the whole band, including Liam and Noelle, were off their nuts on crystal meth."

podcast.title: Dominant British Bands (End of 1994)
podcast.body: By the end of 1994, Oasis was one of three bands dominating the British music scene, alongside Blur and Suede, indicating an impending explosion in the Britpop movement. "As we got to the end of 1994, three bands dominated the British music scene. There was Oasis, there was Blur, and there was Swade."

"The first documented evidence of a public war between Noel and Liam was at a show at a club called Joiners Arms in Southampton on March 29, 1994."

podcast.title: First North American Tour – Offensive Lyrics and Whisky a Go-Go Fight (Fall 1994)
podcast.body: During Oasis's first North American tour, Liam began changing song lyrics to be offensive, greatly annoying Noel, as they were his compositions. This culminated on September 29, 1994, at the Whisky a Go-Go in Los Angeles, where Noel's insistence on singing harmonies annoyed Liam, leading to multiple on-stage confrontations and Liam hitting Noel with a tambourine, refusing to return for the encore. "Liam started by changing the words of some of the songs into something rather offensive. This greatly annoyed noelle because of course they were his songs."

podcast.body: From the release of their first single in April 1994, Oasis was subjected to a relentless schedule of concerts, single launches, album releases, and extensive tours. This intense commercial and label pressure, combined with the band members' youth, frequently led to public controversies, erratic behaviors, and outspoken interviews, with some statements later prompting apologies from the band. podcast.title: Whisky a Go Go Performance and Aftermath (September 29, 1994)
podcast.body: During a performance at the Whisky a Go Go on Sunset Strip on September 29, 1994, Noel's insistence on singing harmonies alongside Liam's lead vocals agitated Liam. They repeatedly confronted each other on stage, culminating in Liam hitting Noel with a tambourine, leaving the stage, and refusing an encore. A backstage fight involving a thrown chair ensued, with Liam seen "skulking down Sunset Boulevard" and Noel departing with $8,000 of band money for Las Vegas and San Francisco, leading to the cancellation of more than half a dozen shows. "On September 29th, 1994, they played the whiskey a go-go on the sunset strip. Noel insisted on singing harmonies to lead lead vocals, which really annoyed Liam. They squared off on stage a bunch of times, and at the end of the set, Liam whacked Noel in the back of the head with a tambourine."

podcast.title: "Battle of Britpop" Single Release - August 15, 1995
podcast.body: Oasis's single "Roll With It" was deliberately released on August 15, 1995, the same day as Blur's "Country House," due to Damon Albarn's strategic move. This generated massive media attention, with even tabloids covering personal lives, the Financial Times running profiles, and the BBC covering it like a major news event. "Damon Alborn started it. When he found out when Oasis was going to release the first single from their What's the Story Morning Glory album, he moved the release date of the new Blur single up to the very same date, August 15th, 1995."

podcast.title: "The Battle of Britpop" Competitor (August 1995)
podcast.body: Oasis directly challenged Blur in August 1995 by moving the release of their single "Roll With It" to August 14, the same day as Blur's "Country House." Despite selling 216,000 copies, Oasis's single was outsold by Blur's. "Oasis said, no, we've decided that we're going to release our single in mid-August."

srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop

podcast.title: Brit Pop Rivalry with Blur (1995)
podcast.body: Oasis was deeply involved in an intense rivalry with Blur, described as a "war" between "Brit Pop's two biggest stars," which significantly hyped the release of Oasis's second album. The conflict began with a near-fight at a San Francisco radio station and escalated when Liam Gallagher and Damon Albarn almost brawled backstage at an award ceremony. Damon Albarn intentionally advanced Blur's single release date to coincide with Oasis's, culminating in the "Record War" of August 14, 1995, involving "Roll With It" versus "Country House," a battle that captivated all of Britain's music and daily papers, with even bookmakers taking bets. "This was much more than a rivalry. This was a war."

podcast.title: Fresh Entry into Britpop (1995)
podcast.body: In 1995, as Britpop reached its peak, Oasis entered the movement with an unstoppable and very fresh energy. This contrasted with Blur, who, despite being pioneers, were already feeling fatigued and pressured by the industry.

And I think it sold for about a thousand US dollars."

This contrasted sharply with Blur's more "burnt out" state during the "Great Battle of Britpop." "Por el otro lado oasis habían lanzado su primer disco menos un año antes, y la aparecía pletórico en 1995."

podcast.body: Both Oasis and Blur planned album releases for Fall 1995: Blur's "The Great Escape" on September 11th and Oasis's "(What's the Story) Morning Glory" on October 2nd. The conflict escalated when Oasis announced their single "Roll With It" for August 14, 1995, and Blur subsequently announced their single "Country House" for release on the exact same day, setting up a direct competition for the number one spot. podcast.title: The Great Britpop Battle (1995)
podcast.body: Oasis played a central role in the highly publicized "Great Battle of Britpop," an event largely manufactured by record labels. This rivalry reached its peak with the simultaneous release of Oasis's "Roll With It" and Blur's "Country House." xref.title: Final Show March 1, 1994; Death April 8, 1994 – The Vacuum That Reshaped 1994's Rock Landscape
xref.body: Nirvana played their final concert in Munich on March 1, 1994 — Kurt's voice was shot, the band was exhausted, and the rest of the European tour was canceled. On March 3, he deliberately overdosed on tranquilizers in a Rome hotel room. On March 18, police were called to his Seattle house after he locked himself in a room with guns. He agreed to enter rehab after an intervention, then escaped. His body was found April 8. The news was read on air: "Nirvana lead singer Kurt Cobain shot himself to death at a Seattle home yesterday." The effect on music fans was profound and prolonged. The loss of Nirvana's central narrative created a temporary opening that Green Day, The Offspring, Blur, and Oasis each rushed to fill. "Kurt's death was extremely traumatic. xref.title: Oasis Tenure
xref.body: In 2004, Zach Starkey joined Oasis as an employee rather than a full member, a status he preferred as it allowed him the flexibility to pursue other projects when not needed by Oasis.
